Answer: F
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates dextrocardia (cardiac apex and gastric bubble on the right side of the patient, which appears on the left side of the image), parallel linear opacities ('tram tracking') in the lower lobes indicative of bronchiectasis, and a gastric air bubble located on the patient's right (appearing on the viewer's left). These findings are characteristic of Kartagener syndrome (primary ciliary dyskinesia with situs inversus).
